title: Supreme Court: CoC Cannot Withdraw an Approved Resolution Plan Once Filed With NCLT
case_name: Bank of India v. S.M. Kamal Pasha
citation: Civil Appeal No. 12045 of 2026, decided 26 October 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court held that a committee of creditors cannot withdraw its approval of a resolution plan once it is before the NCLT, even if the debtor's finances later improve. The NCLT had allowed withdrawal; the NCLAT reversed that for want of jurisdiction, and the Supreme Court agreed. A resolution plan, it held, is not an ordinary contract but draws its binding force from the insolvency statute once approved.
card_tip: An improved balance sheet while a plan is pending before the NCLT is not a ground for the committee of creditors to pull back its approval; raise financial changes before the committee votes, not after.
verification_notes: Confirmed by numerous independent reports (Bar and Bench, LiveLaw, Taxscan, LawChakra and others) agreeing on parties, citation and holding, relying on Ebix Singapore v. CoC of Educomp Solutions; judgment itself not accessed.
